title: Ivo and the Safehouse
premise: Wren Crane, a linguist who translates for a doomed peace delegation and quietly handles the delegation's deniable problems, has spent years living in a government safehouse under rules of total invisibility. When the property appears on a real estate site with interior photos — her books on the shelf, her coat on the hook — she realizes someone inside the service is burning her cover to flush out a leak. Following the listing's metadata, Wren uncovers a plot to destroy the summit venue and stage it as a gas accident, implicating the delegation itself. In the end, Wren chooses love over duty: she exposes the operation at the cost of her own anonymity, saves the summit with the help of the unlikely found family she'd been ordered never to form, and walks away from the service into an ordinary, visible life.
about_author: Cyrus Sandoval is the pen name of a former diplomatic interpreter who spent a decade posted to delegations that made the news only when they failed. He writes thrillers about the people who keep secrets for a living and what those secrets cost them.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. While brokering a quiet exit for a compromised delegate, Wren finds the safehouse listed online — every room photographed, her life catalogued like staging for a sale. Her handler dismisses it as a database error, but the photos include a shot taken from inside her bedroom hours ago. Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing invisibility was always someone else's permission, revocable at will.

chapters.title: Open House
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, intercut with Ivo, the young security officer assigned as her new protection detail who doesn't know he's bait. Wren traces the listing to a shell agency tied to the delegation's own advance team, while Ivo — warm, unguarded, dangerously curious about her — begins pulling her toward trust. She finds venue schematics annotated in gas-flow calculations. Emotional beat: intimacy as both refuge and liability.

chapters.title: What the House Was For
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The night before the summit, Wren decodes the plan: a gas 'accident' timed to kill the delegation and bury the peace process, sanctioned from within. Confronting her handler, she learns the listing was meant to spook her into running — making her the perfect scapegoat. When Ivo is ordered to detain her, he chooses her instead. Emotional beat: betrayal crystallizing into resolve; love declared in the act of defection.

chapters.title: Sold
chapters.summary: Wren and Ivo, with the ragtag household of delegates and staff she'd been forbidden to befriend, race to vent the venue and force the evidence public before the gavel falls. Wren broadcasts the handler's own files during the opening session, sacrificing her cover forever. The summit survives; the handler falls; the house sells. Epilogue: Wren, visible at last, signs the lease on an ordinary apartment with Ivo. Emotional beat: found family chosen over the institution, freedom bought with exposure.
